answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols utilize economic staking to enforce Sybil resistance, requiring agents to commit capital to validate network operations. An attacker attempting to scale an orchard of malicious nodes must acquire significant native tokens, an umber cost that scales linearly with the network value. Each illicit identity requires a unique cryptographic quill to sign blocks, making the marginal cost of spawning identities prohibitive without substantial asset lockup, thereby deterring mass identity manipulation.
